note.p: Ed Pope suggests: Perhaps Joyce Gold printer 103 Shoe-la from 1799 to 1823 (bbti) and bookseller (SunFire 1808), Joyce Gold stationer 5, Gt Eastcheap (SunFire 1812). Also, on 3 April 1821 Godwin notes that Gold (London Magazine) calls on him and on 25 April he calls on Mrs Gold. The London Magazine is in print with January 1821-June 1821 being vol III, when it was published by Baldwin, Cradock and Joy. The 1824 edition was published by Taylor and Henry of Fleet Street. A still further set of publishers is identifiesd as Hunt and Clarke in 1822. No source identifies the printer. The editors (between 1820 and 1824) were John Scott (1783-1821) and John Taylor (1781-1864).

The London Magazine seems to have been re-launched under the new editorial team of 'Thomas Merton' pseud. in December 1824 and published by Charles Knoight - suggesting that Godwin may have been approached by the previous printer of a failing enterprise.
